title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: lsastrat turns large-scale assessment (LSA) data — PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS — stratification inequality quantities education researchers report, returns first-class objects. handles two features make LSA data awkward: Plausible values (PVs). Achievement reported several imputed draws, single score. Every estimator computed PV results combined Rubin’s (1987) rules, measurement uncertainty enters standard error. Replicate weights. Complex sampling means variance must estimated replicate weights (BRR/Fay PISA; JK2 TIMSS/PIRLS) , segregation indices, clustered bootstrap. Inference uses t reference Rubin degrees freedom (normal), matters LSA studies provide 5 10 plausible values.

title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: Consider standard workflow one -reported quantities educational stratification, ESCS gradient set countries. Done hand means: country, fit 10 plausible values x 81 weights = 810 weighted regressions, pool slopes Rubin’s rules, derive strength pooled R-squared, keep track Fay factor – repeat every country, every robustness variant. General LSA packages (intsvy, EdSurvey, Rrepest) automate regression still leave gradient, segregation indices, opportunity decompositions correct inference assembled manually, none applies finite-sample bias correction segregation literature calls . lsastrat one call returning labelled estimate design-correct uncertainty: tidy() turns result publication table, autoplot() figure, lsa_multiverse() robustness analysis. examples use pisa_mini, fully simulated PISA-like data set bundled package (real PISA data). 10 plausible values mathematics reading (PV1MATH…PV10MATH), final weight (W_FSTUWT), 64 Fay BRR replicate weights (W_FSTURWT1…W_FSTURWT64), background variables.
code: lsa_by(stu, by = "CNT", estimator = social_gradient,        achievement = paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH"), escs = "ESCS", design = des) reps <- paste0("W_FSTURWT", 1:64) math <- paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH")

title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: social_gradient() follows OECD definition: slope score-point change per one unit socio-economic index (ESCS), strength percentage achievement variance explains (R² × 100), curvature optional quadratic term. result behaves like model object:
code: g <- social_gradient(pisa_mini, achievement = math, escs = "ESCS",                      weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = reps) g #> Socio-economic achievement gradient #>   SES index: ESCS   |   10 plausible value(s)   |   n = 2048 #>   Variance:  BRR, 64 replicate weights (+ PV imputation); t reference #>  #>  #>           Estimate Std.Error     t    df       p #> slope       41.357     1.831 22.59 399.4 2.1e-73 #> strength    20.189     1.799 11.22 389.1 1.7e-25 #> curvature    1.025     1.597  0.64 406.7 5.2e-01 #>  #> slope = score points per 1 unit of ESCS; strength = % variance explained (R^2 x 100) coef(g) #>     slope  strength curvature  #> 41.357302 20.188700  1.025083 confint(g) #>               2.5 %    97.5 % #> slope     37.758539 44.956065 #> strength  16.651036 23.726363 #> curvature -2.113944  4.164111 plot(g)
